title: Junior Software Developer
descriptionHtml:
The Software Developer I, Connector role supports Trial Interactive’s proprietary platform, Connector - the cloud-based integrations that move life science data between clients’ clinical systems (for example EDC/eCRF and IRT systems) and Trial Interactive’s life science products. Working under the guidance of senior engineers, the role helps build and maintain connectors, keeps client data flowing accurately, and resolves issues when it does not.

This is a blended role, covering development and maintenance up until handling client requests. This role works closely with the Solutions, DevOps and Engineering teams.

DESCRIPTION

As part of the Development and maintenance responsibility, the resource handles:

• Develop, test and maintain connector components in C# on .NET (AWS Lambda), including the parsers and mappers that convert source-system data (API payloads, files) into the formats required by the Trial Interactive CTMS and eTMF.

• Configure and extend mappings for new studies, sites and visit/status definitions on existing connectors, reusing existing modules wherever possible.

• Assist in the technical onboarding of new clients and studies: connector configuration, test runs in non-production environments, and verification before go-live.

• Work with the AWS services connectors are built on (Lambda, SQS, S3, EventBridge/Step Functions, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and make small, reviewed infrastructure changes using Terraform under supervision.

• Consume, test and troubleshoot REST APIs (client/vendor APIs and Trial Interactive import APIs) using code and tools such as Postman, and help extend APIs that improve connector stability and connectivity.

• Write unit and functional tests; use Git (feature branches, merge requests, environment branches) and follow the team’s code review and release process.

• Keep code, configuration and change records documented so that others can maintain them.

• Work on special projects, such as local test environments using LocalStack.

As part of handling Client communication, support and ticket resolution, the resource does:

• Own assigned support tickets from triage to closure: reproduce the issue, investigate, fix or escalate, and record the outcome in the ticketing system (for example Jira, ServiceDesk Plus).

• Investigate data issues end to end – trace a record from the source payload through the archive, parser, connector database and logs to its CTMS/eTMF import result – and establish the root cause (RCA) with evidence.

• Reconcile source-system data against the CTMS/eTMF when a client reports missing or mismatched subjects, visits or statuses, and explain any differences.

• Communicate with clients and Solutions Engineers by email, tickets and calls: acknowledge requests promptly, ask clear clarifying questions, give regular status updates, and explain findings and next steps in plain language.

• Monitor connector health (CloudWatch logs, failed imports, notifications) and respond to failures within agreed response times.

• Escalate appropriately to senior engineers, DevOps or the vendor, with a concise summary of what happened, when, in which environment and for which records.

• Write up RCAs, fixes and known issues so that repeat problems are resolved faster, and help keep support documentation current.

• Handle client and clinical data with care: use the minimum data needed, never share one client’s information with another, and follow Trial Interactive data-protection and change-control procedures.

General

• Keep learning the connector platform, the clinical-trial data domain and cloud and software development best practices.

• Complete all other tasks that are deemed appropriate for this role and assigned by the manager/supervisor.


REQUIRED SKILLS

• Clear written and spoken English, with the ability to explain technical issues in plain language to non-technical clients and to write concise ticket updates and emails.

• A client-service mindset: responsive, calm under pressure, and takes ownership of a ticket until it is resolved or properly handed over.

• Strong problem-solving and debugging skills: forms a hypothesis, checks logs and data, and proves the root cause with evidence before concluding.

• Strong attention to detail with data, such as identifiers, dates, time zones and character encodings.

• Good time management: balances planned development work with interrupt-driven support, prioritizing by client impact.

• Works collaboratively within a team, asks for help early, and is self-motivated and eager to learn.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree or its equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• 0–1 years of experience in software development, technical support or cloud-based application support; internships and substantial academic or personal projects count.

• Working knowledge of C# and the .NET framework: able to read and debug existing code and deliver small features.

• Familiarity with AWS, particularly Lambda, S3, SQS and CloudWatch Logs.

• Working SQL skills (joins, filtering, aggregation) on relational databases, preferably MySQL.

• Understanding of REST APIs and of JSON, XML and CSV data; experience calling APIs with Postman or similar tools.

• Understanding of data parsing and mapping techniques, including handling of dates, null values and encodings.

• Experience or familiarity with version control systems (e.g., Git).

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• Experience with LocalStack for local AWS cloud application development.

• Familiarity with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code tools.

• Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation.

• Prior experience in customer-facing support, or with ticketing tools such as Jira or ServiceDesk Plus.

• Exposure to clinical research systems and concepts (EDC, CTMS, eTMF; study, site, subject, visit) or to regulated (GxP) software environments.

• Scripting (Python or shell) for data checks and log analysis.

• Familiarity with containerization and microservices architecture.

title: Lead AI Product Manager - Telematics
descriptionHtml:
About Zego 🚀

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook.

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

About the Role

We are looking for a Lead AI Product Manager to own Telematics at Zego. Our proprietary telematics is how we understand the way people actually drive, and the ratings it produces shape pricing, risk management and claims across our whole book.

You’ll own the telematics stack as a product: the SDKs that capture driving data, the processing that turns it into trips, events and scores, and the Risk Management capabilities that act on them. You’ll set the 6-12 month direction across these teams and make the build-vs-buy-vs-partner calls on sensors, data sources and models.

You’ll work closely with Data Science, Pricing, Claims and Zego’s Leadership Team, champion an experiment-first culture, and mentor Product Managers across the organisation.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Set the six-to-12-month Telematics strategy across the SDKs, data processing and Risk Management, including the build, buy or partner calls on sensors, data and models.

  • Own data quality at the source, setting the standards for trip recording, location accuracy, battery impact and stability that every score depends on.

  • Own the product side of our scoring models with Data Science, so the score is accurate, explainable and safe to change on a live book.

  • Lead Risk Management, defining how we act on driving behaviour - from price adjustments to interventions and cancellations - balancing loss ratio with fair customer outcomes.

  • Turn driving data into P&L impact with Pricing, Underwriting, Claims and Fraud, through sharper risk selection, fairer prices and better fraud detection.

  • Embed rigorous experimentation as the default operating rhythm, even when changes touch price and live policies.

  • Build reusable AI playbooks, workflows and assets that multiply the whole team’s output, from trip-data analysis to automated data and model monitoring.

  • Coach Product Managers across the organisation, raising the bar for product craft and data capability.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

  • Strategic product leadership. Significant experience leading product strategy across multiple teams or domains in a high-growth environment, with decisions that moved business-level metrics.

  • Data, sensor or ML products. You’ve built products on behavioural, location or sensor data - ideally telematics, mobility or IoT - and understand how signals become models, and models become decisions.

  • Technical depth. Comfortable engaging engineers on mobile SDKs, data pipelines and ML pipelines, enough to make informed strategic bets.

  • Commercial and risk fluency. Deep understanding of pricing levers, risk modelling and loss ratios, and credible with Actuarial, Finance and Leadership.

  • Data mastery. You are as comfortable in Snowflake as you are in a strategy review, and you can interrogate model performance, not just read a dashboard.

  • Experiment-first operator. You have built experiment cultures, not just run individual tests.

  • You work AI-first. You will use AI daily here, and we mean daily. You do not need to arrive an expert, but you do need to arrive curious, experiment fast, and take ownership of getting good quickly. People who wait to be trained will find this uncomfortable.

The Zego ways of working 🏡

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

We also make a point of getting everyone in the same room. Teams come together every quarter, and once a year the whole company does, properly. It's a serious investment and consistently one of the best parts of the year.

Here is what the last one looked like.

Benefits 🎁

💰 Market-competitive salary, benchmarked against your function and reviewed every year.

🏆 Annual performance bonus, linked to company performance and your contribution.

📈 Share options, a real stake in the company and a share in the future you build

🩺 Private medical insurance.

🏖️ Pension, generous holiday, and £1,000 a year to spend on getting to the office or learning something new.

💻 Cutting-edge systems and tools, so you always have what you need to drive your impact.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? We want to hear from you.

Zego, leading the AI evolution in insurance.

About our Machine Learning Business Banking team

We’re building intelligent, data-driven and AI/ML-enabled product experiences that help small businesses feel more in control, make better decisions, and get more value from Monzo.

ML is at the core of how we build and scale our products, enabling Monzo to make better decisions, faster, and helping us serve businesses more effectively.

title: Leader, EMEA Product Support
descriptionHtml:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Leader, EMEA Product Support role manages Benchling support in EMEA. As the team leader (a player-coach role), you’ll manage Product Support Analalyts in Europe and spend roughly 40% of your time directly owning customer issues and our most complex escalations. This role owns live customer-impacting incidents for enterprise pharma and biotech customers, helps shape an AI-first support model, and sits close to CX leadership. Working closely with our Global Support and CX Leadership Teams, you’ll combine team leadership, incident management, and thoughtful AI adoption to help scale a modern, efficient Support organization. 

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and coach your team: run daily regional support operations including prioritization and resourcing, hold regular team meetings and career growth conversations, and build a culture where people feel supported and excited to grow.

  • Partner with the Incident Center of Excellence to mature the incident process (post-incident reviews, closing action items, communication playbooks, severity-based response criteria), and help build and run a sustainable off-hours coverage model, including personally rotating in as an escalation responder.

  • Analyze support metrics (volume, severity trends, time-to-resolution, comms timeliness) to inform staffing and process decisions, and report trends to CX leadership.

  • Drive consistent adoption of AI tools across support workflows, piloting ways to reduce ticket-handling time, surface account context automatically, and free up analyst time for higher-value work.

  • Collaborate with Build, Product, Technical Account Managers, Customer Success, and Professional Services on customer issues and incidents, keep help content and product knowledge current, and represent support at customer-facing events as needed.

  • Work the queue alongside your team: own complex, high-priority, and escalated tickets, serve as a first-line contact for regional escalations, and model the troubleshooting, investigation, and communication standards you expect from others.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experienced leader who coaches with empathy and stays close to the work, with 1+ years of management experience and 5+ years of SaaS support or professional services, or demonstrated leadership, including assigning ticket work and managing queues and resources. Able to personally troubleshoot and resolve complex customer issues.

  • Working knowledge of support and incident tooling and best practices for technical support environments (e.g. Salesforce, Zendesk, JIRA, PagerDuty, or equivalent), plus genuine enthusiasm for AI in support, ideally with hands-on experience piloting or driving adoption.

  • Sound judgment under pressure: prioritizing by urgency, severity, and customer health context, and skilled in customer-facing crisis communication, including what to say, when, and to whom during a live incident, and how to translate root cause into clear RCAs/ISNs.

  • Experience with enterprise-grade support: managing high-stakes accounts holistically, building trust with sophisticated customers, and thinking beyond individual ticket resolution.

  • Strong communicator and customer advocate with a bias toward action, comfortable working independently across departments, remote teams, and external stakeholders. Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences related field recommended (biology, microbiology, genetics, biotechnology, neurology, etc.); research or lab experience is a big plus.

  • Based in the Zurich area, or willing to relocate, and able to work on-site in our Zurich office Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday.

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

title: Manager, Quantum Applications Software
descriptionHtml:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems. 

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries. 

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure. 

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström. 

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact. 

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real. 

Job Summary:

PsiQuantum is building the world’s first useful, fault-tolerant quantum computer. Our applications team focuses on developing algorithms and workflows in the fault-tolerant regime.

We are seeking a Quantum Applications Software Manager to lead a small, high-impact team of Quantum Applications Software Developers. This team builds the software tools and infrastructure that enable the development, evaluation, and deployment of quantum applications for real-world problems.

In this role, you will combine hands-on software engineering with team leadership. You will work closely with quantum algorithm developers and architects to deliver scalable, high-quality tools—such as simulators, resource estimators, and compilation workflows—that are critical to turning quantum algorithms into practical solutions.

Responsibilities:

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

title: Mobile Application Developer - AI Neobank App
descriptionHtml:

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

The Role

We are looking for Android engineers to build the native Android experience for Doit's AI Neobank App.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.

 

What You'll Own

  • Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

  • Create clean mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.

  • Work with product and design to simplify complex user journeys.

  • Integrate backend APIs and ensure mobile flows are stable, secure and reliable.

  • Improve app performance, crash rate, loading states, responsiveness and memory usage.

  • Use analytics, user behaviour and production issues to improve the product.

  • Build AI-assisted mobile experiences only where they genuinely improve the user journey.

 

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

  • Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

  • Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

  • Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

  • Experience integrating REST APIs and debugging production issues.

  • Fast execution, high ownership and strong attention to product quality.

  • App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.

 

Tech Stack

  • Kotlin

  • Jetpack Compose

  • Android SDK

  • Coroutines & Flow

  • SQL / NoSQL

  • TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

 

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Thinks in user journeys, not just screens.

  • Cares about making complex financial products feel simple.

  • Moves fast without creating messy code.

  • Notices UX, performance and reliability issues before users complain.

  • Honest about what they personally built, what was team-owned and what impact they can or cannot claim.

 

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who only want fully defined tickets.

  • Developers who build screens without caring about user experience.

  • People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

  • Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

  • People who exaggerate impact without explaining their actual contribution.

 

Location

This role is based in UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our UK office at least 3 days per week.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round


For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Network Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Position

We are looking for an experienced Network Engineer to join our Network Security team to help us to run, scale and continuously improve our network security infrastructure through hands-on operations, design, and implementation. The ideal candidate would have strong networking fundamentals and experience with security appliances such as firewalls and proxy to join our Network Security team.

Jane Street’s numerous distributed systems are built on an agile, reliable, multi-vendor network infrastructure that supports all traffic profiles, from trading to internet connectivity. Supporting such a large multi-function network requires advanced tooling for monitoring and automation. 

Strong communication and interpersonal skills will be needed to collaborate with colleagues across the firm globally. You will find and resolve issues, plan and execute deployments, and improve systems where possible. In this role, we’ll look to leverage your advanced networking skills and security knowledge to: 

  • Work closely with Network Engineering on design and deployment of security perimeter and adjacent network infrastructure
  • Effectively manage and continuously evolve network segmentation, DMZ, and other aspects of network security
  • Evaluate and lab test new platforms for our network security infrastructure
  • Collaborate with Cybersecurity on detection and mitigation of threats and vulnerabilities on our network
  • Interface with application owners and traders to enable business workflows in a secure way
  • Proactively enhance support by improving network infrastructure observability, scripting, and communicating requirements to our software engineers
  • Improve our network security processes and documentation

A holistic approach to system design is critical for this role. The Networking department prioritizes flexibility, compatibility, and efficiency when crafting solutions, all while seeking ongoing buy-in and feedback from users across the firm. Our firm’s culture prizes intellectual humility, openness, and continuous improvement, which translates directly to the daily work of this team. We’re all partners working towards shared goals and are always looking for the next best idea that will make our work stronger. 

Your strong communication skills and analytical thinking will be invaluable as we support the daily work of our colleagues and keep our systems operating at the highest standard.

About You

  • 7+ years of experience operating and deploying network infrastructure
  • Experience with routing and network protocols (OSPF, BGP, PIM-SM)
  • Experience troubleshooting transport protocols (TCP/UDP)
  • Strong understanding of firewall hardware architecture, performance metrics, and its functional components
  • Experience with firewall configuration and troubleshooting
  • Understanding of Public Key Infrastructure and related technologies
  • Understanding of modern encryption techniques
  • High capacity to learn; we are interested in how you think, not just what you know
  • Ability to context switch, while still being able to prioritize and organize your stack 
  • Ideally experience with overlay networks (EVPN, VxLAN)
  • A flexible and reliable team player who enjoys working in a collaborative environment
  • Proficiency in a programming language is preferred but not required
  • Fluency in English is required

title: Operations Manager – Field Deployment, Logistics & Validation
descriptionHtml:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

The challenge

Our interceptor drone systems are deployed by small teams who must set up, operate and pack up fast, under pressure, far from any workshop. Between a system that works on the bench and one that works in the field, the difference is operations: the right kit in the right case, a checklist nobody skips, a manual operators trust. You will take our ground equipment into the field, see first-hand what slows teams down or breaks, and turn every lesson into a lighter kit, a sharper procedure and a better product.

Missions

  • Run field deployments: set-up, operation and teardown of ground equipment during trials and deployments.

  • Write operational checklists: preparation, set-up, pre-mission checks and teardown, so every team gets the same result.

  • Organize logistics: transport cases, packing lists, shipping and lithium battery transport.

  • Track weight and portability: weigh each subsystem, set targets with engineering, push for kits that are faster to carry and deploy.

  • Lead verification and validation: test plans, trials, acceptance tests and reports against requirements.

  • Produce user documentation: user manuals, quick-start guides, and structured field feedback to R&D.

Required skills

  • Engineering degree or equivalent (systems, mechanical or electronics), with experience in testing, integration or field operations of technical equipment.

  • Strong V&V fundamentals: requirements, test plans, acceptance criteria, test reports.

  • Tools: measurement instruments (multimeter, scales), office and documentation tools, Notion or equivalent.

  • Knowledge of drone or defense field operations; dual-use and lithium battery transport rules (UN38.3, ADR) are a plus.

  • Clear technical writing in English for manuals and checklists; French or Ukrainian is a plus.

  • Field-oriented and organized, available for frequent travel.

title: Ops Readiness & Process Optimisation Lead
descriptionHtml:
Ambition has no passport. That belief is why LemFi exists. We're the financial engine for people the world wasn't built to serve, the millions who move countries to build something better and find the financial system hasn't caught up with them yet. We started with remittances: the money people send home to the people they love. Now we run multi-currency accounts, Savings, eSIMs and Credit. Because staying connected to home and building somewhere new are not two separate things. They never were.

About the role

Change is constant at LemFi, and we wouldn't have it any other way. It's how we keep building for our customers and making sure we deliver what they need. But change only works for customers if the people supporting them are ready for it. This role makes sure our CS, Complaints & Compliance teams go into every launch and change prepared, confident and able to give customers the best support possible.

You'll be the CS, Complaints & Compliance voice in every launch, from first spec through go-live and hypercare, and you'll own the readiness framework that makes being ready repeatable. When a launch exposes a broken or manual process, you'll be the one who drives the fix. You'll work across Product, Engineering, Compliance and our frontline teams, driving change through influence and great planning.

What you'll build and own

  • Build and own the CS, Complaints & Compliance readiness framework: one repeatable go-live standard covering training, knowledge base, saved responses, routing, staffing and escalation paths, signed off before anything ships.

  • Get into Product planning early, so operational impact (contact demand, complaint risk, edge cases) is designed in, not discovered after launch.

  • Run launch readiness reviews and the CS go/no-go, then own hypercare: watch contact drivers in the first weeks post-launch and close gaps fast.

  • Turn launch learnings and contact data into process fixes: remove manual steps, stop repeat contacts and simplify how agents work.

  • Push automation and AI wherever it gets customers a better answer faster, from bot-to-agent handoffs to workflow automation.

  • Keep every process documented, version-controlled and audit-ready.

  • Define and report what good readiness looks like: post-launch contact rate, first-time resolution, complaints per launch and time-to-ready.

Your experience

  • A track record of getting operations ready for product launches in fintech, payments or another regulated consumer business. You've run go-lives and owned the process around them.

  • Process mapping and redesign experience: you can take a messy, multi-team workflow and make it simple, documented and measurable. Lean, Six Sigma or similar is a plus, not a must.

  • Fluent in customer support operations: ticketing tools, knowledge bases, routing, QA and the inputs workforce planning needs from a launch.

  • Working knowledge of UK regulatory expectations on customer outcomes, including FCA complaints handling (DISP) and Consumer Duty.

  • You influence without authority: you get Product, Engineering and Compliance to act on operational risk without trying to own their roadmaps.

  • Comfortable with data: you can pull and interpret contact and complaint data to make the case for change.

Nice to have

  • Experience in cross-border payments or remittances, especially launching across multiple markets or corridors.

  • Hands-on experience bringing AI or automation into support workflows and measuring the impact on customers.


Why join LemFi?

Your work here puts money back into families' pockets. That's the reward, and the weight of it. You'll take on some of the hardest problems in finance alongside people who do their best work when the stakes are real. We move fast and we expect a lot, because our customers can't afford for us to do otherwise. In return you get room to own real problems, global impact you can see, and a team that won't slow you down.

Bring grit and ownership and there's a place for them here. Ambition belongs here, come and show us yours.

Follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram and if you haven't already, download the app on the App Store or Google Play.


Don't feel that you're right for this role, but want to submit your interest in working for LemFi? You can join our talent community to stay in touch for future opportunities.

Recruitment agencies notice

LemFi does not accept unsolicited CVs from recruitment agencies. We work only with agencies on our preferred supplier list, and only when we’ve asked them for their support. Any CVs sent to us outside this arrangement will not incur a fee.

AI in hiring at LemFi

We use AI to cut admin, like notetakers that let interviewers focus on the conversation instead of typing. AI never makes hiring decisions. That responsibility always sits with our hiring teams. Read our AI use policy to see how we use AI and how we expect you to use it too.

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. title: Platform Engineer - Data Resilience and Recovery platform
descriptionHtml:
Build and own a self-service, multi-tenant platform that keeps the critical data of 20+ customers recoverable

Do you like building platforms that other teams consume, at scale, across private and public clouds, with security and tenant isolation as non-negotiables? At Schuberg Philis, the world is shifting from traditional backup to data security and resilience. We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to strengthen our Data Management-as-a-Service (DMS) team and help us build the next generation of our platform.

About the Team

The DMS team builds and runs a shared, fully segregated data resilience platform that serves more than 20 of our customers. Customer teams consume it through self-service, and they handle their own day-to-day backup and restore operations. That means you won’t spend your days on job monitoring, restore tickets or backup schedules. Your customers are internal and external engineering teams, and your product is the platform they build on.

You’ll join a dedicated group of data security experts within our larger Services Team and work closely with our sbp.cloud team, who operate our self-built sovereign cloud solutions. With our plan-build-run approach, you take end-to-end ownership: you design it, you build it, you run it.

The Challenge

Running one platform for 20+ customers means solving the hard problems of platform engineering:

  • Multi-tenancy by design: strict isolation of data, access, and performance between customers, on shared infrastructure.
  • Self-service at scale: APIs, guardrails and automation that let customer teams onboard and operate independently, without tickets.
  • Scale and resilience: 4,000+ protected endpoints and more than 25,000 recovery points generated daily, on a dedicated private cloud spanning multiple availability zones.
  • Heterogeneous workloads: Oracle, MS-SQL, SAP, Sybase, PaaS, container platforms and VMs across VMware VCF, OpenStack, AWS, Azure and Kubernetes.
  • Modern storage back-ends: public cloud services and S3-compatible object storage built on Pure FlashBlade//S and NetApp StorageGRID in our own datacenters, plus a long-term archiving tier.
  • Security first: immutability, segregation and hardening in a highly secure environment where recoverability is the ultimate guarantee.

Your Role

As a Platform Engineer, you take full responsibility for the lifecycle of the platform: architecture, deployment, evolution and reliability. You treat the platform as a product: you improve features, drive innovation and keep the user experience of customer teams in mind. You work closely with technology vendors (primarily Commvault) and push their product teams to improve, while applying standardized guardrails, driving automation and following best-in-class practices.

Your focus is on making day-2 operations simple and cost-effective, so there is room to implement new security features, streamline customer onboarding and enable new projects. You also guide customers in their data protection needs, contribute to RFIs/RFPs, and help scope and design new solutions.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the architecture and lifecycle of a multi-tenant data resilience platform, in line with our plan-build-run methodology.
  • Design and ship self-service capabilities that customer teams use independently, end to end.
  • Automate everything repeatable: deployments, tenant onboarding, configuration and platform operations, using Infrastructure as Code.
  • Ensure platform availability, aiming for 100% uptime and maximum customer satisfaction.
  • Evolve a diverse storage back-end across public cloud and on-prem S3-compatible solutions.
  • Enable customers to protect workloads on VMware VCF, OpenStack, AWS, Azure, Kubernetes and more.
  • Work with vendor product teams and drive their roadmaps.
  • Provide hands-on advisory and technical support, contribute to RFI/RFP processes, and help design new solutions.

Who Are You?

  • First and foremost, you are a platform engineer at heart, and you like building things other engineers rely on. A passion for data protection, security and resilience is a plus, and you’ll grow it here.
  • You enjoy teamwork, thrive on challenges and like collaborating with both peers and customers.
  • You’re comfortable in highly secure, complex environments.
  • You have a solid understanding of multi-tenant architectures and security concepts.
  • You are proficient in Linux and/or Windows ecosystems.
  • You have experience across private (VMware/OpenStack) and public cloud platforms (Azure, AWS).
  • You’re skilled in Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible and/or Chef) and in scripting and automation (Python, Bash, PowerShell, etc.).
  • Experience with data management/protection tools is valuable, whether Commvault, Rubrik or similar, but not a must. We’ll teach you the domain; you bring the engineering craft.

More information?

Do not hesitate to call Maggie: 06 23 75 70 86.

Only application submitted through the website will be considered. 

Everyone we work with and consider working with has a right to equal treatment. The hiring and appraisal process at Schuberg Philis is designed to be thorough and equitable, implementing fair payment, benefits, and opportunities across all demographics. 

It is our desire to be a company that brings together multiple nationalities, cultures, religions, genders, abilities, and talents within and across our teams. We welcome colleagues from diverse backgrounds to join Schuberg Philis and actively support diversity and inclusion in the tech industry.

descriptionHtml:

title: Praktikum im Bereich Customer Success Management
descriptionHtml:

  • Voice of the Customer: Du trägst branchen- und kundenspezifische Bedürfnisse, Wünsche und Hinweise unserer Partnerunternehmen in alle Abteilungen bei voiio weiter.

Das zeichnet dich aus:

  • Studium & Perspektive: Du studierst aktuell und noch für mind. 1 Jahr (langfristige Zusammenarbeit als Werkstudent:in).
  • Analytisches & strategisches Denken: Du arbeitest dich schnell in Zahlen ein und bringst ein gutes Gespür für strategische Zusammenhänge mit.

  • Struktur & Resilienz: Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenverantwortlich und behältst auch in einem dynamischen Start-up-Umfeld stets den Überblick.
  • Teamspirit: Du bist Teamplayer:in, hast Lust auf eine wertschätzende Kultur und spaßige Bürotage mit dem Team.

Wir wissen, dass diverse Teams besser performen. Wenn du dich in der klassischen Arbeitswelt oft nicht repräsentiert fühlst, ist das ein Grund mehr, dich bei uns zu bewerben.

Das bieten wir dir bei voiio:

  • Strukturierte persönliche Einarbeitung und die Möglichkeit, im Team einen wertvollen Beitrag zu leisten
  • Unbegrenzter Zugriff auf unsere voiio-Plattform - von Vorträgen und Freizeitangeboten über Fitnesskurse bis hin zu psychologischer Unterstützung

descriptionHtml:

  • Experience with observability and alerting tooling, such as Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana.

  • Track record of reducing operational burden through systematic reliability improvements, automation, or tooling.

title: Principal Compliance Officer
descriptionHtml:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

PRINCIPAL COMPLIANCE OFFICER

The UK financial crime program is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA. This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end — AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm. You will still work the hard cases. It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with “strategy” in the title.

If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat. You will build the UK program from the ground up, setting the standards the team and the FCA will use. This is consumer-scale payments financial crime work – not a private-banking book – and you’ll sit directly with Product and Engineering. You’ll operate in a small team with a direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer, where scope is broad and process is lean. The measure of success is a program that still works a year later, and the role sits alongside MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design and run the UK financial crime programme: policy, procedures, CDD/EDD, risk rating, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, SAR handling, escalation, QA, and training
  • Turn MLR 2017, POCA, the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, JMLSG, the FCA Financial Crime Guide, SYSC 6.3, and payments/EMI expectations into something operations and product can run
  • Own the UK business-wide risk assessment and keep it honest as the product, customer mix, and channels change
  • Handle complex cases — PEPs, adverse media, sanctions hits, high-risk onboarding, fraud typologies, escalations — then use the queue to fix the framework
  • Stand up first- and second-line controls: documentation, workflows, vendor oversight, quality sampling, MI, and issue management
  • Put UK requirements into the customer journey with Legal, Operations, Product, and Engineering. Be the UK voice in global design decisions
  • Report on quality, residual risk, throughput, and control health, and prepare the program for internal audit, skilled-person reviews, and FCA scrutiny
  • Build the operating model as the team grows.
  • Hire, coach, and set the standard
  • Support MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties as the UK permissions model requires

BASiC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience with financial crime in a regulated UK firm (bank, EMI, PI, payments, or e-money), including substantial KYC/CDD/EDD

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • You will still do the cases, close gaps in a small team, do not wait for a 30-page RACI
  • You know the UK regime well enough to argue a point — MLR 2017, JMLSG, POCA, UK sanctions, FCA expectations — and how it lands in a payments product
  • You have designed or rebuilt a framework, procedure, or control, not only cleared files or written a policy nobody ran
  • You have led people or a workstream. You can defend a risk decision and explain it to the Product without jargon
  • EU financial crime experience
  • Experience with the EU AML package, 6AMLD, EBA guidelines, national transposition, or an EU FIU/regulator, especially on cross-border payments, wallets, or EMI/PI products (useful because X Money will not stay inside one perimeter)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • In-office five days a week; occasional work-from-home when needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

  • Competitive base + equity
  • UK private medical covering GPs and specialists; pension; life insurance
  • 25 days’ paid time off; lunch and dinner allowance

title: Principal, Revenue Marketing (International)
descriptionHtml:
Immuta is the Data Authorization Company, helping the world’s largest organizations control who, and what, can access their data.

The way enterprises access data is fundamentally changing. Organizations are racing to put data to work across analytics and AI, while AI copilots and agents are emerging as an entirely new class of data consumer. Traditional approaches built around tickets, static permissions, and manual approvals were not designed for this speed, scale, or complexity.

Immuta provides the authorization layer for modern data and AI. Our platform enables organizations to provision governed access to data by policy, by request, and dynamically for AI agents, so people and AI can access the data they need while enterprises maintain security, compliance, and control.

For Chief Data Officers, that means making enterprise data dramatically easier to access and use without giving up governance. For AI leaders, it means giving AI agents secure, governed access to enterprise data so they can move from experimentation into production.

Founded in 2015, Immuta is trusted by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies worldwide.

  • Our technology ecosystem includes Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Okta, ServiceNow, Teradata, Alation, Atlan, and Starburst — connecting Immuta to the data, cloud, identity, and enterprise platforms powering modern data and AI environments.
  • Immuta has been recognized by Forbes as a top American startup employer, by Inc. Magazine and Built In as one of the best workplaces, and by Fast Company as one of the world’s most innovative companies.
  • Immuta has raised $263 million from investors including NightDragon, Snowflake, Databricks, ServiceNow, Citi Ventures, Dell Technologies Capital, DFJ Growth, IAG, Intel Capital, March Capital, Okta Ventures, StepStone, Ten Eleven Ventures, and Wipro Ventures.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Immuta’s marketing team sits at the intersection of data, AI, and enterprise growth. We turn a complex, important market problem into clear stories and meaningful connections with the people and organizations Immuta serves. This team brings Immuta’s global story to life in markets around the world. We work across cultures, customer needs, and market dynamics while staying connected to a shared purpose and a high standard of execution. For marketers who enjoy learning quickly, making sense of complexity, and helping a growing company earn trust in new markets, this is an opportunity to have visible impact with a genuinely global team.

As Principal, Revenue Marketing (International), you will help shape how Immuta shows up in markets beyond its home base. title: Principal Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Principal Security Engineer 

London (Hybrid) | Technology & Engineering  | Permanent 

The Role

As a Principal Security Engineer at Capco, you'll lead hands-on security engineering delivery for clients across financial services and other complex environments. Depending on the engagement, you'll lead a technical workstream or operate independently as a Principal specialist. Your focus will span Application & Product Security, Cloud & Platform Security and DevSecOps, underpinned by strong security automation. You'll combine specialist depth with cross-domain judgement, client engagement and secure-by-design engineering. 

What You'll Do 

  • Lead the design, implementation and technical assurance of secure solutions across applications, cloud platforms and delivery pipelines; remain hands-on with complex engineering and integration challenges. 
  • Work directly with clients to understand requirements, lead technical workshops and shape practical security designs, delivery plans and technical proposals. 
  • Embed security-by-design across applications, APIs, cloud workloads and the secure SDLC through threat modelling, CI/CD controls, SAST, SCA, DAST and container scanning. 
  • Build and integrate scalable security automation using scripting, APIs, Infrastructure as Code and policy as code; improve control effectiveness and engineering workflows. 
  • Lead technical workstreams or specialist assignments, assure engineering quality and operational handover, mentor engineers and develop reusable standards and patterns. 
  • Leverage approved AI-enabled tools and automation to enhance security engineering efficiency and effectiveness, ensuring appropriate human oversight, security guardrails and validation. 

What We're Looking For 

  • Proven hands-on security engineering delivery and technical leadership, including secure design decisions, engineering assurance, client engagement and mentoring. 
  • Deep implementation expertise in one or more of Application & Product Security, Cloud & Platform Security or DevSecOps, with working knowledge of the other areas. 
  • Practical experience securing applications, APIs, cloud workloads or engineering pipelines, supported by sound knowledge of threat modelling, vulnerability management and secure SDLC practices. 
  • Experience with at least one major cloud platform (Azure, AWS or GCP) and cloud-native security principles, including an understanding of IaC, containers and workload identities. 
  • Strong security automation capability with scripting, APIs and CI/CD tooling, plus experience with IaC or policy as code and integrating security tools into engineering workflows. 
  • Broad awareness of network and infrastructure security, IAM, monitoring and data-protection controls; able to collaborate with specialists and explain technical trade-offs to clients. 
  • Strong understanding of security standards and best practices, including ISO 27001, NIST and OWASP, with the ability to translate security requirements into practical engineering controls and solutions. 

Bonus Points For 

  • Experience in financial services, energy or other regulated sectors; relevant certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, CCSP or cloud security credentials. 
  • Depth across multiple priority engineering domains; experience in software supply-chain or container security, technical presales, or security engineering for AI-enabled systems. 

Why Join Capco 

  • Deliver high-impact security engineering solutions for leading financial institutions and other major clients. 
  • Work in a collaborative, entrepreneurial consulting culture with continuous learning, training and certification opportunities 
  • Help shape secure digital transformation across financial services and energy. 

Benefits 

We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life: 

  • Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover.
  • Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders.
  • Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement.
  • Family Care: Eight complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care.

  • Extra Perks: Wellhub (Gympass), travel insurance, Tastecard, season ticket loans, Cycle to Work, and dental insurance.

Inclusion at Capco 

We're committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know - we'll be happy to help. 

We value each person's unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration - a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day.

descriptionHtml:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

About the Role

You'll be Vibe's founding security hire. Security has been part of how we build since day one and we're already SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, but nobody has owned it full-time. Ad spend and headcount have both roughly doubled every year since 2022, enterprise partnerships keep expanding, and the more visible Vibe becomes, the more scrutiny comes with it. Now it needs an owner.

You'll define the risk model, set the roadmap, decide what we harden and what we accept, and turn policies into running procedures in code on the paths engineers and AI already use. That work happens in a cloud native ecosystem across AWS and GCP, with most of our services running on Kubernetes, everything as code and a GitOps deployment model.

Reporting to our, Head of Infrastructure, and joining a lean six-person Infrastructure and IT team. You won't do it alone, but you'll be the main contributor, and the person every team turns to on security. Since we joined forces with Walmart, you'll also coordinate directly with their cloud security teams.

What You'll Do

Risk & Governance

  • Map Vibe's risk model across every major system.

  • Set the security roadmap with clear priorities.

Security Engineering

  • Pave the road with guardrails and secure defaults enforced across the engineering tool set.

  • Ship the golden paths so the safe way is the easy one.

  • Harden security across our cloud native ecosystem (AWS and GCP) and third-party providers.

  • Own access management from onboarding to offboarding, and get it to the point where it runs without you.

Detection & Response

  • Prioritize vulnerability findings by real exposure, assign them to the team that owns the code, and follow remediation through to closure.

  • Own security incident response from detection through resolution.

  • Turn manual processes into pipelines that run on their own.

  • Launch and run Vibe's private bug bounty program.

Trust & Compliance

  • Own SOC 2 compliance end to end and maintain current certification.

  • Drive Vibe's future compliance initiatives and requirements.

  • Define Vibe's security posture and make it self-serve so enterprise deals clear security without routing through you.

Security Culture

  • Set clear, practical rules for safe AI use, built into the tools themselves, covering both the AI we ship in our products and the AI our teams work with every day.

  • Run security awareness training and measure behavior changes so the whole company raises its bar.

What You Need

  • Built a security function as a company's first security hire.

  • Write code comfortably and bring deep cloud-native security experience.

  • Managed a compliance framework at scale, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or HIPAA.

  • Managed AI security risk hands on, both in what a company ships with AI and in how its employees use it day to day.

Nice to Haves

  • Ran a private bug bounty program.

  • Ad tech security background, including exposure to US privacy law (CCPA/CPRA, VPPA) in a data-heavy environment.

  • Navigated security through a company acquisition.

Our Values

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You'll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

What We Offer

The pay range for this role is €127,000-€171,000. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.

At Vibe, we want you to build something, own something, and grow fast. Here's how we back that up:

  • Variable pay — Based on real Vibe business goals.

  • Hybrid flexibility — We're in the Heart of Paris and our team is in 3x a week!

  • Health insurance — Full coverage via Alan.

  • Meal vouchers — Via Swile.

  • Annual offsite — The whole team, once a year, somewhere worth the trip.

  • Tech Syncs — Engineering and Product meet in person at least quarterly, worldwide.

Our Interview Process

We respect your time. Here's exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.

  1. Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes. We’ll share more context on the role and team, and learn more about your background and what you’re looking for.

  2. Hiring Manager Interview — 45 minutes. Meet with the person you’d work with directly and dive deeper into your experience, technical background, and approach to the role.

  3. Technical Assessment — 90 minutes. A deeper technical conversation covering core engineering skills, problem-solving, and a technical use case relevant to the role.

  4. Bar Raiser Interview — 30 minutes. Meet with a senior leader at Vibe for a final conversation and an opportunity to ask any remaining questions.

  5. Offer — We move quickly once we’ve made a decision. We don’t let good decisions sit.

Equal Opportunity

Vibe is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate all applicants without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We believe the best ideas come from teams with different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.

Referral Instructions

Being referred? Ask your contact to submit your application directly on your behalf.

descriptionHtml:
What You'll Do

As a Principal Software Engineer - Storage, you will help set the technical direction for Radiant's cloud storage offering and lead the design and delivery of the storage services and data capabilities required to run demanding cloud and AI workloads at scale.

You'll work across object, block, and file storage, data lifecycle, performance, resilience, APIs, and platform integrations. You'll partner closely with product, infrastructure, SRE, networking, and security teams, and with customers running the most demanding storage workloads.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role focused on building storage services that are high-performance, reliable, scalable, and easy to consume, through architecture, code, and the standards other teams build on.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Set the technical vision and architecture for Radiant's storage services, and lead their design and implementation.

  • Design and build storage systems across object, block, and file, including the control plane, the data plane, and integration with existing Radiant services.

  • Translate product and customer requirements into robust architectures, APIs, and technical designs, working closely with the Storage Product Manager.

  • Own the performance, durability, availability, and consistency characteristics of the storage platform, and define the service levels it can credibly meet.

  • Profile, benchmark, and tune throughput, latency, and IOPS for AI training, inference, and other data-intensive workloads.

  • Lead integration of storage with compute, Kubernetes (CSI), networking, IAM, observability, and developer tooling.

  • Design for failure through replication, snapshots, data protection, failure recovery, and safe upgrades at scale.

  • Drive operational excellence with SRE, including capacity planning, observability, incident response, and post-incident improvements.

  • Raise the engineering bar across the organisation through mentoring, design and code review, and technical standards.

 

Your Profile

  • Extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed storage systems or storage-heavy cloud infrastructure.

  • A track record of technical leadership at staff or principal level, including setting direction across multiple teams and delivering complex, high-stakes systems.

  • Strong hands-on engineering skills in one or more systems languages such as Go or similar.

  • Deep technical expertise across:

  • Storage: object, block, and file storage, snapshots, replication, erasure coding, caching, tiering, data lifecycle

  • Protocols & interfaces: S3, NFS, SMB, CSI, NVMe/NVMe-oF, RDMA, POSIX semantics, storage APIs

  • Infrastructure: Kubernetes, containers, high-performance networking, GPU clusters, cloud platforms

  • Reliability: durability, availability, consistency models, consensus, failure recovery, data integrity

  • Observability & security: metrics, logging, tracing, IAM, encryption at rest and in transit, auditability

  • Hands-on experience with technologies such as WEKA, VAST, DDN, Lustre, Ceph, MinIO, Pure Storage, or similar.

  • Understanding of AI and HPC storage patterns, such as large-scale training data pipelines, checkpointing, and high-throughput parallel file systems.

  • Able to reason about trade-offs between performance, durability, availability, cost, and operational complexity.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including clear design documents and explaining complex trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Comfortable working directly with customers on highly technical problems.

 

What You Bring

  • Storage domain expertise: Understand how storage architecture affects application and workload performance, down to the hardware.

  • Engineering excellence: Write and review code that sets the standard for correctness, performance, and maintainability.

  • Architectural judgement: Make sound long-term decisions on systems where data loss is not an option.

  • Technical leadership: Influence direction across teams without relying on authority, and grow the engineers around you.

  • Systems thinking: Understand how storage interacts with compute, networking, and the rest of the cloud platform.

  • Ownership: Drive storage capabilities from design through production, operation, and continuous improvement.

 

Qualities we look for:

  • Set the standard: Every single day, you spot opportunities to constructively shake things up

  • Inspire the change: There's no blueprint for the future. You'll embrace challenges and change

  • You're real and you're true to yourself: We cherish and celebrate diversity so you'll feel right at home whoever you are and whoever you're talking to, you treat everyone the same.

 

Why should you join us?

What sets us apart is our blend of modern technology, competitive benefits, and an open, welcoming work culture that enables our people to thrive.

Here are just some of the great things you can expect from us:

  • 25 days of annual leave

  • A culture that emphasises results over hierarchy, process & ego: we place great emphasis on the quality, ingenuity and creativity of work.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: we value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and a growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Learning Time: we all have dedicated learning time to focus on new skills, projects or interests that lay outside of your day-to-day job.

  • Cycle to Work Scheme: we're committed to building a sustainable business, so we encourage cycling to work.

  • Gympass subscription to a variety of gyms and wellbeing apps

  • Participation in the company shares program

  • Enhanced parental pay & leave

Our process: Talent screen → Hiring Manager → Technical interview (two Principal Engineers) → Whiteboard Session → Final.

Company Overview:

Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built.

We design and operate AI-native cloud platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale. Our infrastructure powers GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems designed for the most demanding environments.

We are not building a generic cloud. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure — from powered land, to compute, to software.

As we scale, we're building this organisation from the ground up. We're looking for people who'd rather build the playbook than inherit one — who are comfortable doing the work themselves as well as directing others, and who can adapt as fast as our strategy does. This is a startup model: attitude and adaptability matter more to us than years of experience or the size of the team you've previously managed.

title: Product Engineer (AI Team)
descriptionHtml:

Lupa is building a category defining product the industry has never seen before.

We are the AI-native operating system for veterinary practices and pet parents, replacing the fragmented, clunky systems vets have tolerated for years with a single intelligent platform for scheduling, client communication, clinical documentation, and AI-driven care guidance. Practices run more efficiently, vets get back to doing what they love, and pet parents feel more connected to their animals health than ever.

The traction speaks for itself: one of Europe's top 100 AI startups with a team of over 80 people, 10x growth in twelve months, the UK market leader, and now charging hard into the US and Europe. We have $25M in funding, 3M+ pets on the platform, and a buzzing HQ in Paddington, London.

AI is not a side project here. Jerry, our AI teammate for vets, launches this month with clinical decision support, a listening mode for live consults, and hands-free voice next. You will ship weekly to real clinics and see the impact directly.

In this role, you will:

  • Build Jerry's clinical guideline library: RAG over vet-approved guidelines using hybrid vector and keyword search in Postgres, so Jerry answers clinical questions only from approved sources and cites the exact lines it used

  • Build Jerry's listening mode: a fast classifier that watches live consult transcripts and triggers Jerry to surface missed charges, tests, or risks in real time

  • Build Jerry's voice mode: a hands-free, voice-first experience for ambulatory vets on the road, where everything is spoken and any change waits for the vet's approval

  • Build long-running and scheduled Jerry tasks: turns that keep running after the vet closes the tab, and scheduled jobs that prepare drafts for the vet to approve

  • Own what you build in production across the TypeScript server and Python AI service: deploys, monitoring, fixes, weekly releases, and a share of on-call

  • Be a trusted reviewer on AI pull requests and write the design docs for new AI features

Your background looks something like:

  • 4+ years of professional software engineering, including at least a year shipping LLM features to real users in production

  • TypeScript in production (Node.js backend and React) and Python in production (FastAPI or similar)

  • Has built with LLM APIs in production: tool calling and agent loops, structured output, prompt and model iteration

  • Deploys and owns code in production: CI/CD, Docker, a cloud platform (AWS ideally), monitoring and fixing live issues

  • SQL and Postgres, with git fluency across branches, rebasing, pull requests, and code review

  • RAG experience: embeddings, hybrid vector and keyword search (pgvector), reranking, citations (nice to have · the first project)

  • Voice AI experience: real-time voice agents, speech-to-text, telephony integration (nice to have)

As a person, you:

  • Are a product engineer first · you care about what ships and how it performs in front of real users, not just whether it works in a test environment

  • Own your code end to end, from design doc to production, and do not consider a feature done until it is monitored and stable

  • Can explain the code you wrote, including the code your AI tools wrote for you

  • Are comfortable in a small team with a big scope, working directly alongside vets, product, and the wider engineering org

  • Are excited to work from our London WeWork office most of the week

  • Value working with people who are kind, ambitious, and pragmatic

What does success look like in 6 months?

  • Shipping to production every week and contributing to on-call

  • Jerry's guideline library v1 is live for pilot clinics: it answers only from approved guidelines, cites exact lines, and passes the clinical team's test questions

  • Listening mode is piloted with at least one clinic, with every suggestion tracked to show the revenue it recovers

descriptionHtml:

Our SaaS platform combines transparent machine learning, predictive analytics, and rating technology to turn complex insurance workflows into scalable, data-driven systems. Insurers use it to model and rate risk up to 10x faster while keeping transparency, explainability, and regulatory trust.

As the product suite expands, we are building an end-to-end platform for pricing, reserving, and forward-looking risk decisions.

Akur8 has 50+ nationalities across 8 global offices and serves 420+ clients across 4 continents. We’re an equal opportunities employer, and we value the different perspectives that help shape better products and decisions.

Insurance companies use Akur8 to decide the price of millions of policies. We are looking for a talented Product Engineer to build the features they rely on to do it.

You will join the Pricing team, which builds the part of the Akur8 platform that Actuaries, Underwriters and Product Owners use to design, test and deploy their rates. Your mission is to scope, design and implement features that automate the rating process at insurance companies, from the first discussion of a client need to the feature running in production.

You will work with Product Managers, Designers, Actuaries and other Engineers to understand how insurers price risk, why they work the way they do, and where software can make them faster and more accurate. A good understanding of modelling, maths and logic is needed for this.

At its core, this is a hands-on software engineering role. You will spend significant time writing code, designing data models, building backend and frontend services, and ensuring the systems you ship are scalable, tested, and maintainable.

With AI being a reliable support for implementation, your main value will come from understanding the business context, the architecture and the data models as these will determine the quality of your deliveries. Our platform runs on AWS with Rust, Java, Python, and Angular. Prior experience with them is a plus.

You will work on the core of the platform from your first weeks and see the impact of your work on real clients.

In this role, you will:
