title: Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default

Founded in 2014 by scientists who met at CERN, Proton was built on the belief that privacy is a fundamental human right. What started as an encrypted email service has grown into an ecosystem of privacy-first products, including Proton Mail, VPN, Drive, Pass, and Calendar, used by millions of people worldwide.

We're profitable, independent, and building for the long term. Free from venture capital control and advertising-driven business models, we focus on what matters most: our users. Our work helps protect digital freedom, from everyday privacy to supporting journalists and activists in challenging environments.

Today, we're an international team of 700+ people, with offices across 9 countries. We have high standards for the people we hire and the work we do. You'll work alongside talented, driven colleagues who challenge each other, take ownership, and care about getting things right.

Explore our open-source projects.

Your impact:

We’re hiring Product Engineers across different levels of experience, from junior to staff engineers. Whether you’re looking to take the next step in your career or already have experience leading complex technical projects, we’d love to hear from you. Your scope and level will reflect your experience and the impact you can bring.

As a Product Engineer, you’ll help shape what we build and own work from understanding the problem through to release and improvement. You’ll speak directly with customers, collaborate with Product and Design, and work across the parts of the stack needed to deliver a complete solution.

What you will do:

  • Understand and shape the problem: Work with Product, Design and customers to understand user needs, question assumptions and decide what is worth building.
  • Own complete features: Turn problems into practical solutions across clients, services and data. Take work through testing, release and improvement, paying attention to usability, performance and behaviour in production.
  • Build effectively with agents: Define clear tasks, provide context and evaluate generated code. Investigate failures, challenge suggestions and make changes yourself when needed.
  • Improve how software gets built: Turn recurring problems into better agent instructions, tests, tools and automated safeguards. Share improvements that help the whole team.
  • Build for trust: Make privacy, security, reliability and maintainability part of your decisions. Verify important failure cases, communicate what remains uncertain and make sound trade-offs about release readiness.

What you will bring:

  • Experience delivering production software: You can explain the problems you solved, the decisions you made and what you learned from maintaining your work after release.
  • Technical depth and adaptability: You have strong expertise and can contribute beyond it. You don’t need equal expertise in every layer, but you understand how your work interacts with the wider system.
  • Practical capability with coding agents: You’ve used agents to deliver working software and can explain how you guide them, improve unsuccessful approaches and verify their output.
  • Code fluency and engineering judgement: You can navigate unfamiliar code, trace behaviour, diagnose problems and make precise changes. You can assess an implementation regardless of who — or what — wrote it.
  • Product judgement: You connect technical choices to user needs, care about the quality of the experience and distinguish a useful reduction in scope from a shortcut that puts users at risk.
  • Ownership and collaboration: You move work forward through uncertainty, explain trade-offs clearly, seek out expertise and take responsibility for the outcome.
  • Technical leadership: You’ve led complex projects through ambiguous requirements, made decisions with lasting consequences and helped other engineers develop their judgement while remaining hands-on.

What we offer:

  • Work that Matters: Millions of people trust Proton with their privacy. We answer only to our users — not advertisers, not investors with conflicting agendas, not governments.
  • A Great Team: Diverse, collaborative, and tight-knit, with people from MIT, Harvard, Stanford, Caltech, Cambridge, ETH, and more.
  • Technology: The right hardware and software to do your best work.
  • Learning & Development: We invest in your growth. Proton is one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career — real challenges, real ownership, from day one.
  • Employee Benefits: Strong health coverage, solid retirement options, generous leave, and wellness support.
  • Stock Options: From day one, you have a real stake in what we're building. When Proton wins, you win.
  • In-Person Collaboration: Offices across Geneva, Zürich, Barcelona, London, and more. You'll spend most of your time collaborating face-to-face.
  • Food: Lunch and snacks on us every day in the office.
  • Transport: We cover public transport, bike allowances, or parking — whichever works for you.
  • Flexible Working: You own your schedule. Outcomes matter more than clock-in times.

Compensation range:

We’re hiring across multiple experience levels for this position, with the following annual gross base salary ranges:

Junior / Mid-level: €45,000–€64,000
Senior: €64,000–€106,000
Staff / Highly experienced: Up to €135,000

Your level and compensation will be determined based on your skills, experience and performance throughout the interview process. We’ll discuss compensation expectations early in the process to ensure alignment.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion:

At Proton, we believe diversity drives innovation and strengthens our mission to provide privacy as a default for all. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical ability, or socio-economic background, feel valued and empowered. We strive to create equal opportunities, promote open dialogue, and support continuous learning to ensure every voice is heard and respected.

If you need any extra support or reasonable adjustments during the hiring process, please let your talent partner know.

Candidate privacy notice:

When you apply for a position, refer a candidate, or are considered for a role at Proton AG ("Proton," "we," "us," or "our"), we store and process your information using Greenhouse, our recruitment platform. Two privacy policies apply to this information, together:

  • Greenhouse's Service Privacy Policy, which governs how Greenhouse, as our data processor, handles and secures the information within their platform.
  • Proton's Recruitment & Hiring Privacy Notice, which governs how we, as the data controller, use, retain, and manage your information.

We use your information to evaluate your suitability for the role you've applied for. We also retain it to consider you for future roles that may align with your background and skills, unless you ask us not to.

Once we no longer have a legitimate business need to process your information, we will delete or anonymize it. If you have questions about how we use or manage your data, or if you'd like to access, correct, or delete it, contact our privacy team at Proton does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from candidates, and we will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from an unsolicited submission, even if the candidate is later hired by Proton.

title: Product Engineering Lead
descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone

Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work — and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

— Grigory


Why Secfix exists

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.


What you'll actually do in the first 3 months

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions — because you've earned it, not because of the title.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.


What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?

After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions — and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — you'll run the technical side of it.

Most of your time stays in the code: you ship every week and own the specs, architecture, and reviews on our biggest projects. As the team grows, you'll take on 1:1s, growth conversations, and eventually managing the team.

Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:

  • Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.

  • Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.

  • Team and hiring. Technical interviews and mentoring now; 1:1s, growth conversations, and the EM role as we grow.

  • AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.

What success looks like

At 6 months: You've led at least 2-3 major projects from spec to production. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.

At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've taken over 1:1s as the team grew, and you're ready to step into the EM role.


How we work

We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.

  • Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.

    To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:

  • Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

  • AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.

  • Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.

  • We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.

This role is for you if:

  • You've led a team technically and made it ship faster. You've set its technical direction, run its design reviews, and interviewed for it — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.

  • You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.

  • You have an exceptional IC track record. You're a senior or staff engineer whose code and designs others build on — and you want to grow into managing, not escape coding.

  • You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.

  • You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations in code reviews and design discussions.

  • You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.

  • You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."

  • You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.


What we're looking for

Required

  • 8+ years as a software engineer at senior or staff level, including 1+ years as a tech lead (formal or de facto) for a team of 3+

  • You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data

  • Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't

  • You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt

  • You lead system design, not just contribute to it: you write the spec, own the architecture, and drive it to production

  • Strong OOP fundamentals; Java Spring Boot, Hibernate, or equivalent

  • Relational database design and SQL optimisation

  • Experience interviewing engineering candidates

  • You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook

  • Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK

Nice to have

  • Some people management and technical interviewing experience

  • Designed a technical interview process from scratch

  • Previous experience at a fully remote company

Interview process

We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:

  • 30 min — Intro call with our talent team

  • 45 min — Interview with Grigory

  • 60 min — Technical interview

  • 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI

  • 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders

Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.


What Secfix gives you

  • Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather

  • Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)

  • Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here

  • Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better

  • Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access

  • Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays

  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage

  • Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish Islands

  • Tech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latest

title: Product Feature Owner ADAS
descriptionHtml:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Product Feature Owner Team

Wayve’s Product & Delivery team turns our AI Driver technology into valuable, scalable vehicle capabilities for global OEM partners. We work at the intersection of customer needs, product strategy and engineering delivery—defining what great looks like, aligning teams around a clear outcome and ensuring that Wayve’s technology can be brought to market safely and effectively.

As part of this team, you’ll take end-to-end ownership of specific Collision Avoidance and Lane Keeping ADAS functionalities. You’ll work closely with OEM customers, product and engineering teams to define feature scope, set performance targets and guide delivery from concept through to production. Your work will directly shape how Wayve’s technology performs for customers and drivers as we progress towards higher levels of autonomy.

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Act as the accountable product owner for specific ADAS features, ensuring they are delivered on time, to the agreed specification and in line with customer and business needs.

  • Partner closely with OEM customers to understand their requirements, represent their needs internally and align expectations without compromising Wayve’s product strategy.

  • Work with feature group owners and engineering teams to define feature scope, specifications, performance targets and delivery plans.

  • Engage throughout feature development, providing early feedback, participating in testing and supporting evaluation and validation activities.

  • Serve as the central point of coordination between OEMs, product and engineering teams, creating clarity, resolving ambiguity and reducing misunderstandings.

  • Identify risks early, manage trade-offs and keep teams aligned as feature requirements, customer priorities and the technology evolve.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

  • Owning the end-to-end lifecycle of ADAS features across Collision Avoidance and Lane Keeping, including Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB), Lane Keeping Assist (LKA), Evasive Steering Assist (ESA), Automatic Emergency Steering (AES) and Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM).

  • Defining and evolving feature specifications in partnership with OEMs, engineering and product teams.

  • Harmonising customer requirements across OEM partners to maximise reusable assets, scalability and efficient feature delivery.

  • Setting clear performance targets and ensuring features meet customer requirements, internal capabilities and agreed delivery specifications.

  • Supporting testing, evaluation and validation to ensure feature quality and readiness for production.

  • Maintaining and evolving the strategic feature roadmap as Wayve’s technology advances towards higher levels of autonomy.

  • Participating in agile planning and delivery rituals, helping teams manage dependencies, risks and priorities effectively.

  • Ensuring feature delivery aligns with relevant automotive quality, safety and compliance expectations.

🙌 You should apply if:

  • You have strong experience specifying and delivering ADAS features from concept through to production, particularly across Collision Avoidance or Lane Keeping functions such as AEB, LKA, ESA, AES or BSM.

  • You understand automotive development processes, including requirements management, the V-model, ASPICE, quality and validation.

  • You are confident working directly with OEM customers: understanding their needs, negotiating requirements and representing their perspective internally while maintaining a clear view of Wayve’s product strategy.

  • You have sufficient technical depth to engage credibly with engineering teams on feature trade-offs, feasibility, testing, evaluation and validation.

  • You are a strong cross-functional collaborator who can bridge technical and commercial perspectives, creating alignment across customers, product and engineering teams.

  • You proactively identify risks and issues before they escalate, balancing immediate delivery needs with the longer-term product roadmap.

  • You are comfortable in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and can bring structure and clarity without adding unnecessary process.

  • Experience shipping complete ADAS features into large-scale automotive production programmes would be valuable.

  • Knowledge of automotive quality, safety and compliance standards—including ASPICE, SOTIF, functional safety, GSR-II and DCAS—would be valuable.

  • Experience with machine learning, LLMs or recent generative-AI methods and architectures would be beneficial.

  • You bring curiosity and a forward-looking approach to developing new ADAS capabilities and advancing the customer experience.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

This is a full-time role based in our Leonberg office. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces and workshops with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes)

  • Competency interviews (HM Interview) 45 Minutes

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (ADAS domain knowledge, Technical Depth and Presentation)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment.

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Product Manager, Device Data Management (Français/Anglais)
descriptionHtml:
Product Manager, Device Data Management (Français/Anglais)

Lieu : Paris, France (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)
Niveau : Senior Product Manager
Équipe : Device Data Management (DDM)
Contrat : CDI

À noter : ce poste est basé en France. Vous devez donc y résider ou être prêt·e à déménager, et disposer déjà du droit de travailler dans l’UE. Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de sponsoring de visa, mais nous l’examinons poste par poste : gardez un œil sur notre site carrières pour les opportunités à venir.

Un français et un anglais courants (à l’oral comme à l’écrit) sont indispensables, et nous vous demandons de soumettre votre CV en anglais.À propos de Kaluza

Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les acteurs de l’énergie à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.

Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel à travers les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En combinant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie quotidienne.

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des innovateurs comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Ce que vous ferez :

Vous serez responsable de la localisation française de Device Data Management (DDM), l’un des domaines produit clés de la plateforme Kaluza. DDM consomme des flux de données internes et externes pour représenter les fournitures, compteurs, registres, relevés et consommations. Il gère aussi les parcours liés à ces entités (par exemple, la mise à jour de la configuration d’un compteur), les API qui exposent les données, les pages front-end qui les présentent aux utilisateurs, ainsi que les calculs de projection et d’extrapolation de consommation. C’est un rôle produit full-stack et très opérationnel : vous interviendrez sur tout le domaine, du modèle de données jusqu’à ce que voient les utilisateurs à l’écran.

  • Traduire les exigences du marché français en spécifications claires : transformer les règles du marché de l’énergie français (Enedis, GRDF, passerelle GRD, règles sur les données de compteurs et d’équipements) en exigences produit détaillées couvrant la conformité réglementaire, les flux de données des équipements et la qualité des données.

  • Travailler en étroite collaboration avec nos clients : collaborer main dans la main avec ENGIE et les futurs clients du marché français pour comprendre leurs besoins et construire les exigences ensemble. Bâtir une relation de confiance telle qu’ils viennent vous voir en premier, et vous appuyer sur cette proximité pour orienter ce que DDM construira ensuite pour la France.

  • Construire, pas seulement spécifier : passer vous-même de l’idée au prototype fonctionnel en interrogeant les données, en esquissant des contrats d’API et en montant des preuves de concept. Nous attendons de vous que vous utilisiez quotidiennement des outils d’IA (ex. Claude Code) comme multiplicateur pour prototyper, investiguer et débloquer des situations, et pas seulement pour rédiger des documents.

  • Aligner les équipes globales et locales, toutes fonctions confondues : travailler étroitement avec l’ingénierie, l’UX, la QA et bien d’autres, avec une influence full-stack, pour que tout le monde vise les bons résultats.

  • Être la personne de référence pour DDM France : faire le lien entre nos équipes globales et locales afin d’éclairer les priorités et la stratégie.

Ce que vous apportez :

Critères essentiels :

  • Une expérience avérée en tant que Product Manager, Business Analyst ou équivalent dans des éditeurs de logiciels, avec un solide historique de localisation réussie de produits logiciels complexes pour des marchés internationaux

  • Un français courant et une grande aisance en anglais : notre plateforme et beaucoup de nos équipes fonctionnent en anglais, vous passez donc facilement de l’un à l’autre

  • De l’aisance dans le travail direct avec les clients : vous savez animer une session de travail avec des interlocuteurs clients, faire émerger le vrai besoin derrière la demande, et garder les décideurs alignés et impliqués

  • Un état d’esprit de bâtisseur et une aisance technique : débrouillard·e et opérationnel·le, vous préférez construire un prototype fonctionnel plutôt qu’attendre la spécification parfaite. Vous êtes à l’aise avec les modèles de données, les bases de données et les API, et vous pouvez tenir une conversation technique. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être ingénieur·e, mais vous raisonnez comme tel·le, et vous êtes aussi à l’aise pour réfléchir à un modèle de données que pour penser à ce que l’utilisateur voit à l’écran

  • Une communication claire et incisive, capable de faire le tri dans le bruit et d’expliquer la complexité technique et de marché à des interlocuteurs variés, clients compris, ainsi qu’une expérience de collaboration avec des équipes pluridisciplinaires (ingénierie, QA, BA, Programme, Delivery, etc.) pour livrer des solutions localisées

Idéalement, vous avez :

  • Une expérience dans le secteur de l’énergie en France : vous connaissez le fonctionnement du marché et ses acteurs clés (ex. Enedis / GRDF), notamment sur les données d’équipements et les flux de marché

  • Une expérience avec des plateformes de gestion de l’énergie ou de services publics (utilities) sur le marché français

  • Une bonne maîtrise des outils d’IA à toutes les étapes du cycle de vie produit, de la découverte et l’idéation jusqu’à la livraison et l’itération

  • Jouer pour gagner : La fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : Dépasser la complexité pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

  • Bâtir la confiance chaque jour : Cohérence, transparence et tenir parole.

  • Assumer les résultats : Une responsabilité totale, dans les réussites comme dans les revers, sans ego.

  • Aller plus loin ensemble : Collaboration, respect et diversité des points de vue.

 

Nos avantages

 

  • Rémunération & protection : Bonus discrétionnaire, mutuelle Alan, prévoyance (assurance vie et décès x3) via Alan, et cotisations standard de Sécurité sociale (retraite, allocations familiales, assurance chômage)

  • Indemnités : Remboursement de 50 % des frais de transport domicile-travail, indemnité de télétravail de 200 € et budget formation de 150 €

  • Congés & flexibilité : 25 jours de congés + jours fériés + jours de RTT, congés « Moments That Matter », congé pour événement familial, deux jours de bénévolat rémunérés, flexibilité dans l’organisation du travail et éligibilité à un congé sabbatique (Career Break)

Venez comme vous êtes

 

Nous voulons rencontrer des personnes de tous horizons. Plus nous sommes inclusifs, meilleur sera notre travail, et nous reconnaissons les talents sur la base du mérite et du potentiel. Si le poste vous enthousiasme mais que vous ne cochez pas toutes les cases, nous serions quand même ravis de vous lire.


Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur notre page carrières et sur LinkedIn. Notre politique de protection des données des candidats est disponible ici.

Compensation: €45K – €60K

title: Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Core Experience Team 👋
The Core Experience team looks after how our customers find and book rail travel across the UK and Europe. Our work covers search, supply from carriers and the booking experience, all in service of our purpose of empowering greener travel choices and connecting people and places. We are a collaborative group who enjoy learning from our customers and from each other.

This is a brand new role, created to own what happens once a customer has found the right journey and moves towards booking: reservation details, optional extras and payment. Because it sits so close to the point of purchase, it offers a direct line to customer experience and revenue, and plenty of room to grow. You will work alongside our Search team and the Supply and Payments platform teams, with colleagues in commercial, design, data and engineering, to make booking simple and reliable for customers in every market we serve.

In this role as the Product Manager, Booking Conversion, you will...🚄

  • Own the customer experience from the moment someone chooses a journey to a confirmed booking, setting clear goals for conversion (the share of customers who complete their booking) and revenue while enabling other teams with a stake in the journey.

  • Run quick cycles of experimentation by forming hypotheses, testing ideas, learning from the results and iterating, while shaping a longer-term vision and roadmap for the booking journey.

  • Use customer insight and data to understand where people hesitate or leave, and decide where to invest limited team capacity across each step of the journey.

  • Build a deep understanding of how rail works in different markets and with different carriers. Decide when a market or carrier specific improvement is the right investment, and when to bring ideas and learnings together across markets so that value grows for customers everywhere, rather than staying in one place.

  • Balance wider business goals from other teams, such as adding new supply, increasing booking features for each carrier, and introducing optional extras and new revenue streams, against keeping the journey simple and low in friction for customers.

  • Partner closely with the Supply, Search, New Business, and Payments platform teams, alongside design, data and engineering, to align priorities and deliver improvements together.

  • Communicate openly with a wide range of stakeholders, including commercial colleagues, explaining the reasoning behind decisions and sharing progress and results in a way that builds trust.

  • Bring AI tools into your everyday work, such as prototyping, analysis and delivery, and help the team grow in confidence using them.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Experience improving conversion in a digital booking, checkout or purchase journey, using data to spot opportunities and measure the impact of your changes.

  • Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, and turning what you learn into the next set of improvements.

  • A customer-first mindset, with the ability to combine customer insight and data to make confident decisions even when information is incomplete.

  • Confidence setting direction for a product area, balancing near-term improvements with a longer-term vision.

  • Clear, thoughtful communication, with the ability to explain complex trade-offs and build alignment between teams who may have different priorities.

  • Comfort weighing limited capacity against competing demands, and explaining what you will focus on and why.

  • Ideally, experience balancing local needs with a wider shared strategy, for example across several markets or with third-party suppliers. It is also helpful if you are familiar with travel, ticketing or payments.

  • You may also be curious about AI tools and keen to use them to prototype ideas, analyse results and speed up delivery.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

title: Product Manager - Post Booking
descriptionHtml:
About BlaBlaCar

BlaBlaCar is the world’s leading community-based travel app enabling 40 million active members to share rides across 41 countries each year. Its technology matches drivers with empty seats with passengers heading the same way, so they can share the cost of the trip.

BlaBlaCar’s mission is to be the go-to marketplace for shared travel, bringing carpooling, buses, and trains together in one place. Globally, the BlaBlaCar Group also includes Obilet, the leading online bus ticketing platform in Turkey. By partnering with over 20,000 operators, the Group offers a wide choice of affordable and sustainable transport solutions.

In 2025, the BlaBlaCar community connected 2.7 million meeting points worldwide and enabled 138 million connections between travelers. Drivers saved 568 million euros by carpooling, and all of the BlaBlaCar Group’s mobility services contributed to avoiding 4 million tonnes of CO2 emissions.


Your Mission

As the Product Manager for Post-booking, you will shape the experience passengers have after making a booking, from managing their trips to getting the help they need before, during and after their journey.

You will make post-booking a clear, reliable and useful part of the end-to-end BlaBlaCar experience across carpooling, bus and train. You will help passengers feel informed and in control, while reducing friction for our Customer Relationship Teams (CRT) and supporting the growth of our multimodal marketplace.

You will co-lead the Post-booking squad with an Engineering Manager and work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Customer Relationship and our supply stakeholders.


Your Responsibilities
  • Shape the post-booking vision and roadmap: Set a clear direction for the passenger experience after purchase, translating BlaBlaCar’s product strategy and business priorities into a focused roadmap. Take full responsibility for your scope, from strategy through execution.
  • Improve the post-booking passenger experience: Identify opportunities to strengthen passenger satisfaction and trust by helping people find the information they need, manage their bookings and feel supported throughout their journey. You will lead the end-to-end product discoveries for those opportunities.
  • Optimize CRT contact rate: Partner with CRT teams to understand why passengers get in touch. Improve information on the platform and self-service so passengers can resolve issues with less effort. In particular, you will take over product leadership of our member-facing AI assistant.
  • Use insights to guide decisions: Bring together customer feedback, product data and business context to identify opportunities, set priorities and evaluate impact using appropriate KPIs.
  • Build alignment across teams: Act as the go-to product partner for Post-booking topics. Communicate the strategy, formalize major decisions and align leadership, Engineering, Design, CRT and other stakeholders.

    • Your Qualifications
  • Experience: 3+ years in Product Management, ideally in a consumer marketplace, travel, mobility or another complex transactional product. Experience building products across markets, platforms or service types is a plus.
  • Customer problem-solving: A track record of simplifying complex journeys and helping customers make confident decisions.
  • Analytical approach: Comfortable combining product data, customer feedback and operational insights to identify problems, set priorities and measure results.
  • Cross-functional influence: Able to bring Product, Engineering, Design, Operations and business stakeholders together around clear decisions and outcomes.
  • Languages: Full fluency in English is mandatory.

title: Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Deine Mission

Produkt und Design sind bei Bling eine Rolle.Du baust bei uns eigene Features, vom User-Problem bis zum Release. Du findest das Problem, entwickelst das Konzept, gestaltest die Lösung selbst in Figma und briefst sie übergabereif für die Entwicklung. Nach dem Launch schaust du dir an, wie dein Feature genutzt wird, und entscheidest, was als Nächstes passiert.

Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem Head of Product und trägst vom ersten Monat an die Verantwortung für deine Features.

  • Du hast schon etwas gebaut und kannst es zeigen: ein Feature, ein Side Project, eine App. Ob aus ein bis zwei Jahren im Product Management oder Product Design oder aus starken Praktika, ist uns egal

title: Creator Marketing Manager:in (Performance) (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Wir sind fravio, die Community-Centric Agency aus Köln. Wir bringen Marken und Menschen zusammen: mit Creator- und Influencer-Kampagnen, Street Generated Content® (SGC) und eigenen Communities wie dem onmasportsclub® (OSC) und unserem Kölner Stadt-Account. Community ist unsere DNA, Performance steckt in allem, was wir tun. Profitabel seit dem ersten Jahr und ohne Investoren arbeiten wir für Marken wie Wolt, Vodafone und XING. 2026 haben wir bei The Best Agency Bronze als Newcomer gewonnen und stehen zweimal auf der Shortlist „Agency of the Year“.

Vorab, damit du es einschätzen kannst: Die Stelle ist keine Einstiegsposition. Wir suchen jemanden, der schon selbst Creator ausgewählt, gebucht und Honorare oder Nutzungsrechte verhandelt hat, auf Agentur- oder Markenseite. Wenn du bisher vor allem Content produziert, Community Management oder SEO gemacht hast, passt die Stelle noch nicht.

Aufgaben

Deine Rolle

„Performance“ heißt bei uns: Du kaufst Creator ein, deren Content als Werbeanzeige Neukunden bringt. Den größten Teil deiner Zeit wählst du Creator aus, buchst sie und verhandelst Honorare und Nutzungsrechte, vor allem für Creator-Assets, die unsere Kunden als Dark und Spark Ads schalten, zum Beispiel für Wolt. Du schaust gemeinsam mit dem Kunden auf die Ad-Zahlen und entscheidest daraus, welche Creator und welcher Content als Nächstes kommen. Dazu kommen Awareness-Kampagnen. Außerdem planst du Social-Content für deine Kunden: Du verstehst, welche Trends gerade funktionieren, und übersetzt sie strategisch für die Marke und ihre Zielgruppe. Selbst im Ads-Manager steuerst du nur bei einzelnen Kunden. Das musst du nicht schon perfekt können, das lernst du bei uns.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Content-Planung: Du planst Social-Content für deine Kunden und richtest ihn an Marke, Ziel und Zielgruppe aus.

  • Trends & Strategie: Du erkennst früh, was auf TikTok und Instagram funktioniert, und übersetzt Trends strategisch für deinen Kunden und seine Zielgruppe.

  • Creator-Einkauf: Du findest passende Creator, buchst sie und verhandelst Honorare, Nutzungsrechte und Paid Usage (Spark Ads, Whitelisting) eigenständig.

  • Briefing: Du brieftst Creator so, dass der Content als Ad funktioniert, prüfst Skripte und stimmst dich mit unseren Produktionen ab.

  • Content zu Ads: Du entscheidest, welche Assets als Dark oder Spark Ad laufen, und lieferst sie an den Kunden aus.

  • Auswertung: Du liest die Ad-Zahlen (CPM, CTR, Hold Rate, Kosten pro Neukunde) und die Kommentarspalten und leitest daraus die nächste Creator-Auswahl ab.

  • Ad-Steuerung: Bei vereinzelten Kunden planst, schaltest und optimierst du die Kampagnen auf Meta und TikTok selbst.

  • Kundenkontakt: Du stellst Ergebnisse vor und vertrittst deine Empfehlungen beim Kunden.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

  • 2–3 Jahre Erfahrung im Creator- oder Influencer-Marketing, gern auf Agenturseite oder im Creator-Programm einer Marke.

  • Du hast Creator selbst ausgewählt, gebucht und Honorare oder Nutzungsrechte verhandelt.

  • Du verfolgst Social-Trends und kannst begründen, warum ein Format zu einer Marke und ihrer Zielgruppe passt.

  • Du weißt, warum ein Creator-Video als Ad funktioniert (Hook, Hold Rate, CTR), und hast schon mit Ad-Zahlen gearbeitet, egal ob du selbst geschaltet hast oder eng mit einem Performance-Team.

  • CPM, CTR, ROAS und Conversion-Rate liest du nicht nur, du triffst damit Entscheidungen.

  • Du wohnst im Raum Köln oder ziehst her.

  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch und fließendes Englisch.

Schön, wenn du schon selbst im Meta- oder TikTok-Ads-Manager gearbeitet hast, Dark und Spark Ads umgesetzt hast und mit Pixel und Conversions API vertraut bist.

Benefits

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Verantwortung: Du kaufst für einen unserer größten Accounts Creator eigenständig ein und entscheidest mit, wer als Nächstes gebucht wird.

  • Growth: Raum für deine Entwicklung in Richtung Senior oder Unit-Verantwortung. Wer bei uns wächst, bekommt Perspektive: Verantwortung als Führungskraft im Team oder fachlich im eigenen Thema.

  • Hybrid: flexible Arbeitszeiten, Homeoffice und Office, mittwochs ist unser Office Day.

  • Team: kurze Entscheidungswege und Sparring direkt mit den Gründern.

  • Equipment und Perks: MacBook, modernes Office im Herzen von Köln, Jobticket, regelmäßige Teamevents.

So bewirbst du dich

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und zwei, drei Sätze zu einer Creator-Buchung, die du selbst verhandelt hast: wofür, zu welchen Konditionen, was dabei herauskam. Wir melden uns innerhalb von 2 Werktagen.

title: Propulsion GSE Team Leader
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecraft for humanity.


We are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refueled in orbit, and which carries cargo - and potentially humans in the longer run.

We are seeking an experienced and talented Propulsion Ground Support Equipment Team Leader, to lead the development, commissioning and operation of our engine test benches that we use to test our cryogenic engines and storable thrusters.

This is a key leadership role that requires technical expertise in liquid-propellant propulsion systems, a strong track record in managing complex engineering projects, and proven experience in leading and mentoring technical teams. The GSE Team Leader role for Liquid Propulsion Testing drives the end-to-end lifecycle – from initial concept and fluid/structural design to fabrication, commissioning, and operation – of critical ground infrastructure supporting liquid propellant rocket engine test campaigns.

As the GSE Team Leader, you will oversee the design, development and building of propulsion test facility. The primary objective is to develop and maintain robust, high-reliability test bench GSE that meets ambitious program cadences while ensuring absolute safety in hazardous operating environments.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the engineering development of new test facility GSE, including high-pressure gas distribution systems, propellant feed systems, electrical network, control and data acquisition system, mechanical structures, etc.

  • Translate test matrix requirements into hardware specifications, master P&IDs, and fluid system architectures

  • Manage a cross-functional team of mechanical, fluid, and instrumentation engineers and technicians

  • Direct resource allocation across multiple test benches, manage development schedules, and ensure alignment between propulsion design teams and facility operations

  • Oversee the structural fabrication, tube bending, welding, and mechanical assembly of GSE lines, panels, and thrust measurement structures

  • Lead high-pressure proof testing, leak checks, and system commissioning/decommissioning phases

  • Establish protocols for handling hazardous fluids (both cryogenic and storable propellants)

  • Enforce strict compliance with oxygen compatibility, system passivation, and precision cleanliness levels

  • Manage data acquisition and control systems (DAQ/DCS) engineers and technicians to integrate sensors (pressure transducers, thermocouples, flow meters) and remote-actuated valves into the GSE infrastructure for automated test sequences and redline monitoring

  • Author structural and fluid safety calculations, hazard analyses, and standard operating procedures

  • Maintain rigorous configuration control of test pad setups to ensure repeatable test conditions and audit readiness.

Required Qualifications & Skills:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering

  • Equivalent technical experience with a proven track record in complex fluid systems engineering may be considered

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in rocket propulsion testing, launch pad operations, or high-pressure chemical processing plants

  • At least 2 years of experience leading engineering or technical teams

  • Advanced proficiency in developing and interpreting complex fluid schematics (P&IDs)

  • Strong working knowledge of industrial fluid component selection (valves, regulators, check valves, etc.)

  • Experience with 3D CAD modeling (NX, CATIA, or SolidWorks) for GSE packaging

  • Experience with fluid simulation tools

  • Knowledge of precision cleaning techniques for aerospace applications

  • Decisive leadership under high-pressure testing schedules

  • Exceptional risk-assessment capability

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey technical concepts to diverse audiences

  • Capacity to travel to test sites and partner facilities as required

  • Fluency in English.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. 
 
The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. title: QA Lead - Data Platform (TL1)
descriptionHtml:
Location: Bristol or London

Level: TL1

Team: Quality

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Shira Tsinovich

 

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

 

About Kaluza

 

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

 

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

 

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

 

What you’ll do


As the QA Lead across Data you will work closely with the Data Org, setting the testing approach and quality standards for its products and platforms.

You will be the quality partner for data delivery teams, advising on testing and quality assurance across the software delivery lifecycle. You will work with Data Engineering, Product teams, and clients to make sure changes meet the defined quality bar before they reach client environments.

This is an individual contributor role with no line management responsibilities. You will influence through expertise, relationships, and evidence.

  • Define and own the test strategy and test plans for the Data Org, deciding what is tested and how, based on risk, criticality, and impact to the business and clients.

  • Create and deliver test plans for complex data systems, covering functional, transformation, schema, and ETL/migration testing, plus end-to-end coverage across data and engineering teams.

  • Set the quality gates that determine whether a change is fit to be promoted to client environments, and assess release readiness against milestones.

  • Ensure defects are logged, triaged, prioritised, and tracked to resolution in accordance with Quality standards, and drive root-cause analysis on recurring or high-impact issues.

  • Select and maintain the tools and frameworks used for testing, with automated checks running in CI/CD.

  • Work with delivery teams, programme teams, and clients to support queries on test data and releases, and to maintain client confidence through clear, professional communication.

  • Influence engineers, data analysts, and leadership to adopt a test-first mindset and own the quality of their products, and hold a firm line on quality standards.

  • Report on test progress, quality trends, and risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders, and raise delivery risks and blockers early.

  • Maintain documentation of quality standards, test coverage, and decisions, with transparency on known issues and risks.

  • Act as the subject matter expert on data testing and data quality practices, including data quality checks (completeness, accuracy, consistency, uniqueness, validity, timeliness).

What you’ll bring

  • Proven QA and testing experience: Strong knowledge of QA strategies, processes and methodologies, including defining and executing test plans, test cases and test scripts for complex software applications.

  • Agile, test-first delivery: Experience in cross-functional Agile teams with a test-first mindset, managing priorities, scope and risk to maximise testing impact across distributed engineering organisations.

  • Data testing and SQL: Working knowledge of data testing methods (data quality checks, schema validation, transformation testing, ETL/migration testing), plus SQL proficiency for querying and profiling large datasets to diagnose quality issues.

  • Quality metrics and reporting: Experience building quality metrics, dashboards and reporting for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Collaboration and communication: Strong stakeholder management and verbal and written communication skills, working with development, product and client teams at all levels of management, including client engagement.

  • Influence and coaching: Ability to influence and negotiate across engineering, product and leadership, hold a firm line on quality standards, and coach engineers and product managers to own the quality of their products.

  • Client Delivery: experience working directly with client teams to define and report quality metrics, and to introduce quality improvement plans.

  • Nice to have: Test automation framework experience; defining quality gates in CI/CD or release pipelines; AI tools for identifying and fixing data issues; data testing and observability tooling; familiarity with data governance, data contracts and GDPR; and Python and visualisation tools (e.g. Power BI, Looker).

Our Values

 

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

 

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

 

Our Perks

 

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

 

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

 

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Quality Assurance Inspector (All Genders)
descriptionHtml:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Production Quality team in Thessaloniki is the technical shield protecting the integrity of STARK’s next-generation autonomous systems. Operating directly on the production floor, we partner with assembly leads, technicians, and engineering teams to stand up resilient, high-yield manufacturing processes. We bridge precise structural mechanical builds with complex, high-reliability aerospace-grade electronics. We value absolute technical precision, structured problem-solving, and the proactive ownership required to safeguard zero-defect manufacturing standards.

YOUR MISSION

As our Quality Assurance Inspector, you will be the final gatekeeper of production standards on our assembly floor. Utilizing your combined knowledge of mechanical and electronics engineering, you will continuously review active assembly lines, verify build documentation, and ensure all mandatory inline steps are executed flawlessly. You will take end-to-end ownership of on-floor quality checks—collaborating closely with Manufacturing Engineers to identify assembly gaps, block defective parts, and update localized Control Plans so our processes are continuously improved.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Conduct rigorous inline quality checks on active production lines, verifying that electro-mechanical sub-assemblies, wire harnesses, and avionics conform exactly to design schematics.
  • Review assembly lines to identify physical gaps, actively collaborating with Manufacturing Engineers to implement tooling, jig, or process improvements.
  • Define, update, and maintain dynamic Control Plans (CPs) for inline assemblies and final products based on real-time assembly data.
  • Block defective products immediately, physically isolating and managing quarantined materials on the floor.
  • Initiate and coordinate technical reworks, providing on-floor guidance to technicians and verifying that repaired systems meet original engineering standards before re-release.
  • Perform final quality checks and outgoing document reviews before delivery, recording deviations in the QMS and creating precise Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Education: Vocational diploma or technical degree in mechatronics, electronics, mechanical assembly, or a related field.
  • Experience: 3+ years as a Quality Inspector, QA Specialist, or Lead Assembler in aerospace, automotive, or defense.
  • Technical Skills: Strong practical understanding of both electronics (wiring, connectors) and mechanics (tolerances, fasteners, blueprints).
  • Process Review & Control Plans: Proven ability to spot floor assembly gaps, collaborate with Manufacturing Engineers, and execute dynamic Control Plans (CPs).
  • NCR Ownership & Languages: Experience managing non-conformances in QMS/ERP with professional working proficiency in English and Greek.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Active certifications in IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 standards.
  • Familiarity with flight-critical avionics systems (flight controllers, power distribution boards, telemetry) or military-grade hardware, tactical defense systems, and UAS.
  • Familiarity with ERP/QMS platforms (SAP QM, JIRA, CAQ) and basic training in Lean manufacturing, Kaizen, or Six Sigma.

If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, and you see yourself reflected on the description above, please send us your CV in English. We're looking forward to meeting you!

SECURITY CLEARANCE

Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

About 9fin

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.

Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.

The Opportunity

9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets, the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion. Debt markets are vast, global and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis and high-value workflows across global markets.

Today, 9fin powers teams at 350+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.

We are bringing Client Engagement together as a single global function under our Global Head of Client Engagement. We are hiring Regional Directors to lead it on the ground. You will own retention, adoption and growth for your region (EMEA or the Americas), lead a team of Client Engagement Managers across a tiered coverage model, and turn client insight into action across the business.

This is a role for a proven CS or AM leader who wants to scale a function. You will inherit a strong foundation, shape the next stage, and be accountable for commercial outcomes: gross and net revenue retention, product adoption, and the health of our most important client relationships.

What You’ll Work On

Every day is different, but here is the kind of work you will lead:

Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead, coach and develop a regional team of Strategic CEMs, Senior CEMs and Client Engagement Managers across the whole region, and the managers beneath you as the team grows.

  • Run a tiered coverage model: Strategic CSMs for our most important accounts, Senior CSMs for key accounts, and CSMs for the wider base. Define clear roles, service levels and career paths at each level.

  • Hire, onboard and train to a rapid growth plan, with a strong bench of internal successors.

Retention, Adoption & Growth

  • Own regional gross revenue retention (GRR), with clear early-warning signals and remediation plans for at-risk accounts.

  • Drive seat-level adoption: activate and re-activate users, build champion networks, and embed 9fin in each client’s daily workflow.

  • Lead adoption of our newest products, including 9fin AI and Private 9fin, with client-specific programmes and measurable usage goals.

  • Design role and client-specific adoption metrics that forecast usage trends, so the team drives usage proactively.

  • Partner with Account Management and Relationship Managers on renewals and expansion, with clear ownership at each stage of the client lifecycle.

Strategy & Operating Model

  • Translate the global Client Engagement strategy into a regional plan, with the playbooks, success plans and lifecycle programmes to execute it.

  • Use health scoring and usage data to decide where the team spends its time, and to move accounts between coverage tiers as their needs change.

  • Report regularly on regional KPIs to global leadership: retention, adoption, health, renewals and expansion pipeline.

Voice of the Client

  • Represent clients in conversations with Product, Engineering, Data and Editorial, backing requests with evidence such as the accounts affected, the ARR at stake and the workflow impact.

  • Work with our Forward Deployed team on strategic accounts, setting shared success criteria and feeding what you learn back into the product.

  • Build executive relationships with senior stakeholders at your region’s most important clients.

Operational Excellence

  • Use Salesforce, our analytics tools and client engagement platforms to make the team more proactive, with automation where it frees up time for high-value work.

  • Keep playbooks, client communications and dashboards current, and create feedback loops that improve the client experience.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 3 months: a clear picture of your region’s accounts, risks and team, and a regional plan agreed with the Global Head of Client Engagement.

  • Within 6 months: accounts assigned and covered under the tiered model, with health scoring in use and a visible improvement in early-warning response.

  • Within 12 months: measurable gains in regional retention, adoption and AI and Private 9fin usage, and a team with the capacity and leadership depth to keep scaling.

Requirements

This role will be a great fit if you have:

Experience & Expertise

  • 8+ years in Customer Success, Account Management or related client-facing roles in Capital Markets, Enterprise B2B SaaS or Financial Data, including 3+ years leading teams.

  • Experience managing AMs, CSMs, AEs or building the layer of leadership beneath you, ideally across more than one region or client segment.

  • A track record of scaling or structuring a CS or AM function through a period of fast growth.

  • Strong understanding of global financial markets, and credibility with buyside, sellside and advisory clients.

Commercial Acumen

  • Proven success driving retention, adoption and expansion in enterprise accounts, ideally accountable for a portfolio of $50m in ARR.

  • Comfort being measured on GRR, NRR and adoption, and designing the KPIs, dashboards and forecasting that support them.

  • Experience working alongside sales and account management on renewals and expansion, with clear ownership between teams.

Leadership & Communication

  • Excellent people leadership: you coach, develop and hold a high bar for high-performing teams.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders both inside 9fin and at clients.

  • The judgement to prioritise competing demands and to use data to decide where the team focuses.

Bonus Points

  • Existing relationships in the Leveraged Finance, Debt Capital Markets or Restructuring community.

  • Experience in a high-growth fintech or data provider, or with seat-based professional data products.

  • Experience driving adoption of AI products or working with embedded or forward deployed teams.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce, product analytics and client engagement platforms.

Why Join Us?

You will join a fast-moving, ambitious team helping to power the largest financial market in the world. This role offers the chance to lead a regional Client Engagement team at a pivotal moment: with a clear global strategy, a product that clients rely on daily, and the mandate to shape how we retain and grow our client base for years to come.

Benefits

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Financial & Insurance

  • Competitive Salary (our salary bands are benchmarked at the top end of the market)

  • Equity

  • Pension (your minimum contributions are 4% with 9fin matching up to 7%)

  • Private Medical Insurance

  • Paid sick leave with Income Protection for long periods of illness

  • Group Life Assurance

  • Season Ticket Loan & Cycle to Work schemes

Time off

  • 25 holiday days per year

  • Local public holidays (with the ability to exchange them for alternative days)

  • Work abroad for up to 3 months a year

  • 1 month paid sabbatical after 5 years of service

  • Enhanced parental leave & flexible working arrangements available

Growth & Culture

  • Professional learning and development budget

  • AI experimentation budget of £800 (UK) per employee to trial AI tools

  • Quarterly team socials

  • Summer and Winter company social events

 

Hybrid Policy

9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role.

9fin is an equal opportunities employer

At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might just be who we’re looking for — either for this role, or perhaps another.
